kb/Work PB358 LANDED 2026-09-09. RULE: 'Data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 may be qualified.' (cite.py --check 14.9.30.3 OK.)
WHY CONFORMS RATHER THAN PARTIAL: the same discriminator as SR-14.9.30.3-11. data-name-1: 'readKey : KEY IS? dataReference' routes the operand through the general dataReference rule, so the whole qualification apparatus (OF/IN chains) applies, and BindRead resolves it through ctx.Refs.Resolve(keyRef) like any other reference; the qualified form 'KEY IS IX-ALT OF IX-REC' was probed and returns the alternate-key record. The measured underlining on printed page 722 backs the spelling accepted here - KEY required and IS optional - which 'KEY IS?' matches, and kb/Work PB331 confirmed that measurement while re-deriving the whole figure; conformance:cases/14.9.30-READ/pb331_read_lock_brackets exercises the unqualified form in all three printed spellings.
record-key-name-1: the qualified record-key-name is 8.4.6 Format 6 (qualified-record-key-name), a DISTINCT syntax rather than a spelling of the data-name half - and it is unreachable because a record-key-name cannot be declared at all: Annex A.3 item 40's SOURCE phrase is declined (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 40) and, since 2026-09-09, refused BY NAME as COBOL1954 with five conformance:negative/pb358-* witnesses at 85/2002/2014/2023. SR-14.9.41.3-7 owns that decline and carries DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT. A rule whose subject is a claimed facility conforms once its declined operand class is diagnosed rather than tripped over (the discriminator the owner set on SR-12.4.5.9.3-1, kb/Work PB371).
